title: Vote early in person or by mail (absentee voting)
question: How do I vote early or get a mail ballot in Albemarle?
office: Department of Voter Registration and Elections (General Registrar)
summary: Registered Albemarle County voters may vote absentee without giving a reason, early in person or by mail. Early voting needs no application: for the November 3, 2026 election it runs from September 18 to 5:00 p.m. Saturday, October 31 at the 5th Street County Office Building (1600 5th Street Extended, Room A), with weekend hours; bring ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement. For a mail ballot, apply online or on the state form so the office receives it by 5:00 p.m. on October 23, 2026. Return it to the drop box by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day, or mail it postmarked by Election Day to arrive before noon Friday, November 6. Errors that would void a ballot received by October 30 can be cured by then.

legal_basis.quote: Any registered voter may vote by absentee ballot in accordance with the provisions of this chapter in any election in which he is qualified to vote.
There shall be in each county and city an electoral board composed of three members who shall be qualified voters of such county or city.
Each electoral board shall meet in the month of May or June in 2007, and every four years thereafter, and shall appoint a general registrar
The following officers shall not, except as herein otherwise provided, be affected by the adoption of the county executive form:
Absentee voting in person shall be available on the forty-fifth day prior to any election and shall continue until 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday immediately preceding the election.
An application shall not be required for any registered voter appearing in person to cast an absentee ballot pursuant to § 24.2-701.1 .
Any registered voter offering to vote absentee in person shall provide his name and his residence address in the county or city in which he is offering to vote.
The officer shall ask the voter to present any one of the following forms of identification:

If he does not show one of the forms of identification specified in subsection B of § 24.2-643 , he shall be allowed to vote after signing a statement, subject to felony penalties for false statements pursuant to § 24.2-1016 , that he is the named registered voter he claims to be.
A voter who does not show one of the forms of identification specified in this subsection or does not sign this statement shall be offered a provisional ballot under the provisions of § 24.2-653 .

For purposes of this chapter, such offices shall be open to the public (i) a minimum of eight hours between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the first and second Saturday and (ii) a minimum of five hours between the hours of 11:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on the second and third Sunday immediately preceding all elections.
Any applicant who is in line to cast his ballot when the office of the general registrar or voter satellite office closes shall be permitted to cast his absentee ballot that day.
The governing body of any county or city may establish, by ordinance, voter satellite offices to be used in the locality for absentee voting in person.

Not later than 55 days prior to any election, the general registrar shall post notice of all voter satellite office locations in the locality and the dates and hours of operation of each location in the office of the general registrar and on the official website for the county or city.

An application for an absentee ballot may be accepted the later of (i) 12 months before an election or (ii) the day following any election held in the twelfth month prior to the election in which the applicant is applying to vote.

An application that is completed in person at the same time that the applicant registers to vote shall be held and processed no sooner than the fifth day after the date that the applicant registered to vote
The registration records shall be closed during the 10 days before a primary or general election.

any person who is qualified to register to vote shall be entitled to register in person up to and including the day of the election at the office of the general registrar in the locality in which such person resides or at the polling place for the precinct in which such person resides.

Any other application may be made by mail, by electronic or telephonic transmission to a facsimile device if one is available to the office of the general registrar or to the office of the Department if a device is not available locally, or by other means.
The application shall be made to the appropriate registrar no later than 5:00 p.m. on the eleventh day prior to the election in which the applicant offers to vote.
The applicant's printed name and the last four digits of the applicant's social security number.
Any registered voter shall be eligible to file a special application to receive absentee ballots for all elections in which he is eligible to vote.
A voter shall be removed from the permanent absentee voter list if (i) the voter requests in writing to be removed from the list

The application for an absentee ballot shall provide space for the applicant to indicate that he will require assistance to vote his absentee ballot by reason of blindness, disability, or inability to read or write.

On receipt of an application from an applicant who indicated that he will require assistance due to a visual impairment or print disability, the general registrar shall offer to provide to the applicant a ballot marking tool with screen reader assistive technology made available pursuant to § 24.2-103.2 .

the general registrar shall not reject the application of any individual because of an error or omission on any record or paper relating to the application, if such error or omission is not material in determining whether such individual is qualified to vote absentee.
The general registrar shall note on each application received whether the applicant is or is not a registered voter.

The general registrar shall make printed ballots available for absentee voting not later than 45 days prior to any election or within three business days of the receipt of a properly completed absentee ballot application, whichever is later.
An envelope, properly addressed and postage prepaid, for the return of the ballot to the general registrar by mail or by the applicant in person, or to a drop-off location.

Such individual who desires to vote by mail but who does not submit one of the forms of identification specified in this paragraph may cast such ballot by mail and the ballot shall be counted as a provisional ballot under the provisions of § 24.2-653.01 .

After the voter has marked his absentee ballot, he shall (a) enclose the ballot in the envelope provided for that purpose, (b) seal the envelope, (c) fill in and sign the statement printed on the back of the envelope, (d) enclose the ballot envelope and any required assistance form within the envelope directed to the general registrar, and (e) seal that envelope.

A voter's failure to provide the date, or any part of the date, including the year, on which he signed the statement printed on the back of the envelope shall not be considered a material omission and shall not render his ballot void.

A mailed absentee ballot shall be returned (i) by mail to the office of the general registrar, (ii) by the voter in person to the general registrar, or (iii) to a drop-off location established pursuant to § 24.2-707.1 .

For purposes of this subsection, "mail" includes a delivery by a commercial delivery service but does not include delivery by a personal courier service or other individual except as provided by §§ 24.2-703.2 and 24.2-705 .
Failure to follow the procedures set forth in this section shall render the applicant's ballot void.

The general registrar of each county or city shall establish at the office of the general registrar and each voter satellite office in operation for an election a drop-off location for the purpose of allowing the deposit of completed absentee ballots for such election.
On the day of the election, there shall also be a drop-off location at each polling place in operation for the election.

Not later than 55 days prior to any election, the general registrar shall post notice of the sites of the drop-off locations in the locality in the office of the general registrar and on the official website of the county or city.
Absentee ballots shall be returned to the general registrar or to a drop-off location before the closing of the polls.
Any voter who is in line to return an absentee ballot at a drop-off location by 7:00 p.m. on the day of the election shall be permitted to deposit his absentee ballot.

any absentee ballot (i) returned to the general registrar after the closing of the polls on election day but before noon on the third day after the election and (ii) postmarked on or before the date of the election shall be counted pursuant to the procedures set forth in this chapter if the voter is found entitled to vote.
For purposes of this subsection, a postmark shall include any other official indicia of confirmation of mailing by the United States Postal Service or other postal or delivery service.

The voter shall be entitled to make such necessary corrections before noon on the third day after the election, and his ballot shall then be counted pursuant to the procedures set forth in this chapter if he is found to be entitled to vote.

The voter may, prior to the day of the election, return the ballot to the general registrar (i) unopened in the sealed envelope in which it was sent to him or (ii) opened and unmarked.
The voter may, on the day of the election, return his unused ballot to his proper polling place or central absentee voter precinct, and the unused ballot shall be preserved with other unused ballots.

The voter may, on the day of the election, offer to vote at his proper polling place or at a central absentee voter precinct without returning his unused ballot, and he shall be entitled to cast a provisional ballot pursuant to § 24.2-653.1 .

Any person who has applied for and has been sent an absentee ballot but does not receive the ballot or loses the ballot shall be entitled to cast a ballot in accordance with the provisions of this subsection.

the voter may request a replacement absentee ballot by the close of business for the local elections office on the Saturday before election day

Any person registered and otherwise qualified to vote may request at any time prior to 2:00 p.m. on the day preceding the election that he be permitted to vote by emergency absentee ballot with the assistance of his designated representative.

will be unable to vote on election day due to his hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness, or death of a spouse, child, or parent, or other emergency found to justify receipt of an emergency absentee ballot that occurred after the deadline for applying for an absentee ballot

The ballot shall be counted only if the ballot is received by the general registrar prior to the close of polls, and the general registrar shall deliver the ballot to the officers of election at each appropriate precinct pursuant to § 24.2-710 .

A qualified voter may vote absentee in person in the office of the general registrar through 2:00 p.m. on the day immediately preceding the election by complying with the requirements of § 24.2-643 and affirming that one of the following emergency circumstances will prevent him from voting on election day:

After 12:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election, an obligation arose that requires the voter be absent from his county or city on election day for (i) his business, profession, or occupation; (ii) the hospitalization of the voter or a member of his immediate family; or (iii) the death of a member of his immediate family.
The Secretary, in coordination with local election officials, shall implement a free-access system by which a voter may determine:

The electoral board of each county and city shall send a written explanation of the reason for rejection of an absentee ballot to the voter whose absentee ballot is rejected within 90 days of the date on which the ballot is rejected.

An officer of election, by a written notice given to the voter, shall inform him that a determination of his right to vote shall be made by the electoral board and advise the voter of the beginning time and place for the board's meeting and of the voter's right to be present at that meeting.

The electoral board shall meet on the day following the election and determine whether each person having submitted a provisional vote pursuant to § 24.2-653 was entitled to do so as a qualified voter in the precinct in which he offered the provisional vote.
A central absentee voter precinct shall be made by the governing body by ordinance; the ordinance shall state for which elections the precinct shall be used.
The circuit courts shall have jurisdiction to issue an injunction to enforce the provisions of this section upon the application of (i) any aggrieved voter

The State Board, through the Department of Elections, shall supervise and coordinate the work of the county and city electoral boards and of the registrars to obtain uniformity in their practices and proceedings and legality and purity in all elections.

The State Board may institute proceedings pursuant to § 24.2-234.1 for the removal of any member of an electoral board or general registrar by a recorded majority vote of the Board after a public hearing on related matters.

Any willfully false material statement or entry made by any person in any statement, form, or report required by this title shall constitute the crime of election fraud and be punishable as a Class 5 felony.
The following omissions are always material and any Envelope B containing such omissions shall be rendered invalid if any of the following exists:
The voter did not provide the voter's house number, street name, or rural route address;
The voter did not provide either the voter's city or zip code;
The voter did not sign Envelope B;
The voter did not provide the voter's birth year; or
The voter did not provide the last four digits of the voter's social security number
The voter omitted the date, or provided an incorrect or incomplete date on which the voter signed Envelope B;

If there is no evidence from the Intelligent Mail barcode that the ballot was mailed after the close of polls for the relevant election and if the return envelope has a missing postmark, the ballot shall be rendered invalid.

steps.step: Make sure you are registered to vote in Albemarle County at your current address
steps.how: Check your voter record on the Virginia Citizen Portal, or call the Department of Voter Registration and Elections at 434-972-4173. Absentee ballots come from the registrar of the county or city where you are registered; the City of Charlottesville has its own registrar. For the November 3, 2026 election the county lists October 23, 2026 as the registration deadline, with same-day registration in person from October 24 through Election Day (the rules are in the voter registration process). If you register in person and apply for a mail ballot at the same time, the application is processed no sooner than the fifth day after you registered.
steps.deadline: Registration deadline October 23, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election (same-day registration from October 24, 2026 through Election Day)

steps.step: Choose how to vote: early in person, by mail, or at your polling place on Election Day
steps.how: No reason is needed to vote absentee. Early in-person voting needs no application. A mail ballot needs an application for each election, unless you join the permanent absentee list, which sends you a ballot for every election you are eligible to vote in until you ask in writing to be removed (form ELECT-703.1D, or Section 6 of the change form SBE-703.1C), your registration is cancelled or made inactive, or you move out of the county.

steps.step: Early in person: go to the 5th Street County Office Building during the early voting period
steps.how: Early voting is at the 5th Street County Office Building, Room A, 1600 5th Street Extended, Charlottesville, VA 22902; no other early voting site is listed. For the November 3, 2026 general election the county's schedule is Monday to Friday from Friday, September 18 through Friday, October 30, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; Sunday, October 18 and Sunday, October 25, 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; Saturday, October 24, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; and the last day, Saturday, October 31, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Anyone in line when the office closes may still vote that day. You can vote early only in the county or city where you are registered.
steps.deadline: Early voting ends at 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election (Saturday, October 31, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)

steps.step: Early in person: give your name and address, show ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement, and vote
steps.who: Voter; officers of election and the registrar's staff at the early voting site
steps.how: Give your name and residence address. Show an acceptable ID (the county lists, for example, a Virginia driver's license, a U.S. passport, an employer-issued photo ID, a student photo ID from a U.S. college or a Virginia high school, or a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck or government document with your name and address), or sign the ID Confirmation Statement. A voter who does neither is offered a provisional ballot and may send the electoral board a copy of ID or a signed statement by noon on the Friday after the election. The Department of Elections says accessible equipment and curbside voting are available on request at early voting; the county's Election Day page offers curbside voting at polling places to voters 65 or older and to anyone with a physical or mental disability.
steps.quote: At the early voting location, you must provide your name and address and show an acceptable form of ID or sign an ID Confirmation Statement.

steps.step: By mail: apply for a mail ballot
steps.how: Apply online through your Virginia voter record on the Citizen Portal; the county says you need your Social Security number and Virginia driver's license, because the online application uses your DMV signature. Or complete the paper Virginia Absentee Ballot Application (SBE-701/703.1) and send it to Voter Registrations and Elections, 1600 5th Street, Charlottesville, VA 22902 by mail, as a scan emailed to VoterRegistration1@albemarle.org, or by fax to 434-972-4178. Call 434-972-4173 to have a paper form mailed to you. The form asks for your name, the last four digits of your Social Security number, your registration address, the election you want a ballot for (Section 3), a different ballot mailing address if you want one (Section 5, not used with the permanent option), and your signature. Check Section 7c if you need help marking the ballot, or to receive it electronically if you are print-disabled. Answer Yes in Section 4 to join the permanent absentee list. An application may be accepted from 12 months before the election (or, if later, from the day after any election held in the twelfth month before it).
steps.deadline: Received by 5:00 p.m. on the 11th day before the election (October 23, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)

steps.step: By mail: the registrar reviews the application and mails the ballot
steps.who: General Registrar (Department of Voter Registration and Elections)
steps.how: The registrar notes on the application whether you are a registered voter. An error or omission that is not material to whether you are qualified to vote absentee cannot be a reason to reject the application, but the state form warns that an application without the last four digits of your Social Security number will be denied. If the application is properly completed and signed and you are registered in your precinct, the registrar sends the ballot by first-class or expedited mail with proof of mailing: the ballot, Envelope B with the Statement of Voter, a postage-paid return envelope and instructions that list the drop-off locations, plus an assistance form if you asked for help. The law requires ballots to be available no later than 45 days before the election (or within three business days of a properly completed application, if that is later); the Department of Elections says ballots can be mailed starting 45 days before the election. An application received before the ballots are printed is held until they are available.
steps.deadline: Ballots made available not later than 45 days before the election, or within three business days of receiving a properly completed application, whichever is later
steps.quote: The general registrar shall make printed ballots available for absentee voting not later than 45 days prior to any election or within three business days of the receipt of a properly completed absentee ballot application, whichever is later.

steps.step: By mail: track your application and ballot
steps.how: The Citizen Portal shows whether your application was received and accepted, and later when your returned ballot is checked in at the county elections office. Ballot Scout follows the ballot through the U.S. Postal Service. If the ballot does not arrive, call 434-972-4173 or email VoterRegistration1@albemarle.org.

steps.step: By mail: mark the ballot and complete Envelope B
steps.who: Voter (and an assistant, if you asked for help)
steps.how: Mark the ballot privately and seal it in Envelope B. Fill in and sign the Statement of Voter on Envelope B: your full name, your residence address (house number and street or rural route, city and ZIP code), your signature, the last four digits of your Social Security number and your birth year. The ballot is invalid if the statement leaves out your signature, your full first name (a first initial is accepted with a full middle name), your last name, your house number and street or rural route, both your city and your ZIP code, your birth year or the last four digits; a missing middle name, a missing city or ZIP code when the other is given, or a missing or wrong date does not void it. For a ballot received by the Friday before the election, such a defect can be corrected (step s10). If you asked for assistance, complete and sign the assistance form sent with the ballot and return it with the ballot. If the packet includes a notice that you must send ID (some first-time voters who registered by mail), put a copy of an acceptable ID in with the ballot; otherwise the ballot is counted as a provisional ballot. Put Envelope B (and any assistance form) in the return envelope and seal it.
steps.quote: After the voter has marked his absentee ballot, he shall (a) enclose the ballot in the envelope provided for that purpose, (b) seal the envelope, (c) fill in and sign the statement printed on the back of the envelope, (d) enclose the ballot envelope and any required assistance form within the envelope directed to the general registrar, and (e) seal that envelope.

steps.how: Mail it in the pre-addressed, postage-paid return envelope, or send it by a commercial delivery service such as FedEx or UPS to Voter Registrations and Elections, 1600 5th Street, Charlottesville, VA 22902 (the county says the same deadlines apply). Or put it in the Ballot Drop Box in front of the main entrance of the 5th Street County Office Building, open around the clock from 45 days before Election Day until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day; use the postage-paid envelope there too. The county says ballots cannot be handed to anyone and must go in the drop box, and that you may drop off another voter's ballot as well as your own. On Election Day there is also a drop-off location at each polling place. A ballot that reaches the registrar or a drop-off location before the polls close counts however it was sent; only a mailed ballot arriving after the polls close needs an Election Day postmark. A late-arriving ballot with a missing postmark is invalid; with an illegible postmark the registrar checks the envelope's Intelligent Mail barcode and then the date on Envelope B.
steps.deadline: Received by the registrar or at a drop-off location before the polls close at 7:00 p.m. on Election Day (anyone in line at a drop-off location at 7:00 p.m. may deposit the ballot); a ballot by mail or commercial delivery arriving later counts only if postmarked on or before Election Day and received before noon on the third day after (Friday, November 6, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)
steps.fee: None for U.S. mail: the return envelope is postage paid

steps.step: If the registrar finds a problem with your returned ballot, correct it (cure)
steps.who: General Registrar notifies; the voter corrects
steps.how: For a ballot received by the Friday before the election (October 30, 2026), if the registrar finds that the Statement of Voter was not filled out correctly or completely, or a step required by Va. Code § 24.2-707 was missed, and the error would make the ballot void by law, the registrar records the issue and, within three days of finding it, tells you in writing or by email how to fix it. The registrar may issue a new ballot. Contact the office promptly at 434-972-4173 or VoterRegistration1@albemarle.org. No notice duty was found for ballots that arrive after that Friday.
steps.deadline: The registrar notifies within three days of finding the problem; the voter corrects it before noon on the third day after the election (Friday, November 6, 2026 for the November 3, 2026 election)
steps.quote: Within three days of such finding, the registrar shall notify the voter in writing or by email of the error or failure and shall provide information to the voter on how to correct the issue so his ballot may be counted.

steps.step: If you change your mind, or your mail ballot never arrives or is lost, vote in person instead (or ask for a replacement ballot)
steps.who: Voter; General Registrar or officers of election
steps.how: Changed your mind: before Election Day you can return the ballot to the registrar unopened, or opened and unmarked, and then vote a regular ballot at the office during early voting or at your polling place on Election Day (if the officers cannot confirm the return on Election Day, you vote a provisional ballot). On Election Day you can bring the unused ballot to your polling place; an election official voids it and you mark a new ballot. If you go to the polls without returning it, you vote a provisional ballot. Ballot never arrived or lost: give the registrar or an officer of election a signed statement before Election Day and vote a regular ballot; at the polls on Election Day without that statement, you vote a provisional ballot. A voter with a disability or illness whose ballot did not arrive or was lost by the Saturday before the election may instead ask for a replacement ballot by the close of business that Saturday, naming in writing a representative who collects it and returns it by the close of the polls. The law also lets these voters use the central absentee voter precinct on Election Day; its Albemarle location was not found. Polls are open 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
steps.deadline: Unused ballot returned, or lost-ballot statement given, before Election Day; replacement ballot requested by close of business Saturday, October 31, 2026; early voting ends 5:00 p.m. that Saturday; polls open 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day

steps.step: In an emergency after the deadline, ask for an emergency absentee ballot
steps.who: Voter; a designated representative; General Registrar
steps.how: Emergency absentee ballot (ELECT-705, Section 1b): you may use it if (i) your hospitalization or illness, or the hospitalization, illness or death of your spouse, child or parent, or another emergency, kept you from applying by the deadline; (ii) such an emergency that occurred after the application deadline will keep you from voting on Election Day; or (iii) you applied in time but your ballot had not arrived within 10 days of the election and such an emergency will keep you from the polls. Your designated representative (18 or older, and not an elected official, a candidate, or the deputy, spouse, parent or child of one) witnesses your signature, returns the form, receives the ballot from the registrar, watches you mark it and returns it. Emergency in-person voting (Section 1a): if after 12:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election an obligation arose that requires you to be away from the county on Election Day for your business, profession or occupation, your own or an immediate family member's hospitalization, or an immediate family member's death, or you are an officer of election assigned after that time to a precinct other than your own, you may vote in person at the registrar's office through 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election, showing ID or signing the ID statement (Va. Code § 24.2-643).
steps.deadline: Request before 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election; the completed form returned by 5:00 p.m. that day; the ballot counts only if the registrar receives it before the polls close. Emergency in-person voting through 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election
steps.quote: Any person registered and otherwise qualified to vote may request at any time prior to 2:00 p.m. on the day preceding the election that he be permitted to vote by emergency absentee ballot with the assistance of his designated representative.

steps.step: After the election: if your absentee ballot was rejected, you receive a written reason
steps.how: If an absentee ballot is not counted, the electoral board must send the voter a written explanation of the reason. You can also check the ballot's status on the Citizen Portal. No appeal of a rejected ballot was found in the sections read (see escalation for the cure and other routes).
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the date the ballot is rejected
steps.quote: The electoral board of each county and city shall send a written explanation of the reason for rejection of an absentee ballot to the voter whose absentee ballot is rejected within 90 days of the date on which the ballot is rejected.

escalation.next: General Registrar: send a corrected application before the deadline, or vote early in person instead (no application needed)
escalation.deadline: 5:00 p.m. on the 11th day before the election for a mail ballot; 5:00 p.m. on the Saturday before the election for early voting in person
escalation.quote: the general registrar shall not reject the application of any individual because of an error or omission on any record or paper relating to the application, if such error or omission is not material in determining whether such individual is qualified to vote absentee.

escalation.trigger: Mail ballot received by the Friday before the election has a defect that would make it void (for example, no signature, birth year or last four Social Security digits on Envelope B)
escalation.next: General Registrar (cure: correct the Statement of Voter, or vote a new ballot the registrar issues)
escalation.deadline: Before noon on the third day after the election
escalation.quote: The voter shall be entitled to make such necessary corrections before noon on the third day after the election, and his ballot shall then be counted pursuant to the procedures set forth in this chapter if he is found to be entitled to vote.

escalation.trigger: Mail ballot never arrived or was lost
escalation.next: General Registrar or an officer of election before Election Day (signed statement, then a regular ballot), or the polling place on Election Day (provisional ballot, decided by the Albemarle County Electoral Board); a voter with a disability or illness may instead ask for a replacement ballot by close of business on the Saturday before (Va. Code § 24.2-703.2)
escalation.deadline: Statement before Election Day; or at the polls on Election Day, 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
escalation.quote: The voter may, prior to the day of the election, present to the general registrar or officer of election a statement signed by him that he did not receive the ballot or has lost the ballot.

escalation.trigger: Requested ballot not received within 10 days of the election, and the voter's hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness or death of a spouse, child or parent, or another emergency will keep the voter from the polls
escalation.next: General Registrar: emergency absentee ballot delivered through a designated representative
escalation.deadline: Request before 2:00 p.m. on the day before the election; form returned by 5:00 p.m. that day
escalation.quote: has applied to receive an absentee ballot by the deadline but has not received his ballot within 10 days of the election and will be unable to vote on election day due to his hospitalization or illness, the hospitalization, illness, or death of a spouse, child, or parent, or other emergency found to justify receipt of an emergency absentee ballot.

escalation.trigger: Voted a provisional ballot (for example, at early voting without showing ID or signing the ID Confirmation Statement)
escalation.next: Albemarle County Electoral Board, which decides whether the provisional ballot counts at its meeting the day after the election; any provisional voter may attend the meeting, and a voter who voted provisionally for lack of ID may send the board a copy of ID or a signed statement
escalation.deadline: For a voter who voted provisionally for lack of ID: ID or signed statement received by the electoral board no later than noon on the third day after the election (Friday, November 6, 2026)
escalation.quote: to be received by the electoral board no later than noon on the third day after the election.

escalation.trigger: Unhappy with how the office handled an application, a ballot or a visit
escalation.next: Department of Voter Registration and Elections, then the Albemarle County Electoral Board, which appoints the General Registrar and runs elections in the county (it usually meets on the second Thursday of each month at 9:00 a.m.; no separate office channel for the board is published, so write or call through the elections office)

escalation.trigger: The registrar does not process an application or send a ballot as the law requires
escalation.next: Circuit court: injunction to enforce Va. Code § 24.2-706, on the application of an aggrieved voter. The section does not name the venue; the Albemarle Circuit Court, the circuit court for the county, is listed as the likely court
escalation.quote: The circuit courts shall have jurisdiction to issue an injunction to enforce the provisions of this section upon the application of (i) any aggrieved voter

escalation.trigger: The local office or electoral board does not follow election law
escalation.next: Virginia Department of Elections and the State Board of Elections, which supervise local electoral boards and registrars (the Department's contact page links a Virginia Voters' Election Day Complaint Form, and its Voter Forms page links an Online Voter Complaint Form and a paper Voter Complaint Form; under § 24.2-103(E) the State Board may also begin removal proceedings against a general registrar or electoral board member)
escalation.quote: The State Board, through the Department of Elections, shall supervise and coordinate the work of the county and city electoral boards and of the registrars to obtain uniformity in their practices and proceedings and legality and purity in all elections.

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

Snapshot age: the How to Vote copy is from August 14, 2026, before the September 9, 2026 deadline (55 days before the election) for posting voter satellite offices and drop-off sites (Va. Code §§ 24.2-701.2(E), 24.2-707.1(C)). Any satellite office, extra drop box or schedule change announced later is not reflected. The September 16, 2026 Elections page copy mentions no satellite office. Confirm on the live page or by phone.

Start date: Va. Code § 24.2-701.1(A) makes early voting available on the 45th day before an election. For November 3, 2026 that is Saturday, September 19, but the county page and the Department of Elections' Early Voting Office Locations page both give Friday, September 18 (the 46th day). The reason for the earlier start was not found in the index text of § 24.2-701.1.

Weekday schedule: the county lists weekday early voting as "September 18, 2026 - October 31, 2026", but October 31 is a Saturday, listed separately as the last day. The weekday hours are recorded as ending Friday, October 30.

Hand delivery: the county says a returned ballot cannot be handed to anyone and must be placed in the drop box, while Va. Code § 24.2-707(B) lists return by the voter in person to the general registrar as one of the three lawful methods. In Albemarle an in-person return goes into the drop box in front of the building.

Other voters' ballots: the county allows a voter to drop off another voter's ballot in the drop box. Va. Code § 24.2-707(B) excludes delivery by a personal courier or other individual from "mail", but no rule on who may deposit a ballot at a drop-off location was found in the sections read.

Online application: the county says the online application needs the Social Security number and a Virginia driver's license (DMV signature); the Department's page lists a driver's license number or state ID. The Citizen Portal and Ballot Scout (v2.ballotscout.org/albemarle-county/search, which asks for voter details) are not described here; the Department's page links a different Ballot Scout address (ballot.elections.virginia.gov/voter/va/bt/track).

Versions: the index marks Va. Code §§ 24.2-653, 24.2-706, 24.2-709, 24.2-709.1 and 24.2-711.1 "effective until January 1, 2027", § 24.2-653.01 "effective September 1, 2026, until January 1, 2027" and § 24.2-703.1 (permanent absentee list) "effective until July 1, 2027", and holds no successor text. They govern the November 3, 2026 election; re-check deadlines, the cure process and the permanent list for later elections. The index text of §§ 24.2-701.1, 24.2-705, 24.2-706 and 24.2-707.1 already includes 2026 amendments (per their history lines).

Local law not read. Va. Code § 24.2-712(A) requires the Board of Supervisors to set up the central absentee voter precinct by ordinance, and § 24.2-701.2(A) lets it create voter satellite offices by ordinance. The County Code is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, so no County Code text was read or quoted. Legistar item 18-271 (County Code Chapter 2 rewrite, 2018) describes County Code §§ 2-101 through 2-107 as covering magisterial districts, precincts and polling places; whether one of them establishes the central absentee voter precinct was not confirmed. A search of Legistar matter titles for absentee, satellite, precinct, election and voter found no satellite office ordinance. Legistar item 20-136 (2019 proposal to lease space for the elections office because of early voting) is background only and is not quoted.

Fees: no source read states a fee for applying for or voting an absentee ballot. The cost of returning a ballot by FedEx, UPS or another commercial service is not stated; the postage-paid envelope covers U.S. mail.

Rejected applications: the state form's Privacy Act notice says an application will be denied without the last four digits of the Social Security number. No statute read requires the registrar to notify an applicant whose mail ballot application is rejected, and no appeal route for a rejected application or a rejected ballot was found. The routes recorded are a corrected application or in-person voting, the cure process, the electoral board's written explanation after the election (§ 24.2-711.1(B)), complaints to the office, the electoral board or the Department, and an injunction under § 24.2-706(G).
Cure coverage: the notice duty in § 24.2-709.1(C) covers ballots received by the Friday before the election (October 30, 2026); how the office handles defects on ballots received later was not found.

ID list: the county's Election Day page copy is from March 2026 (it still lists the April 21, 2026 special election). Its ID list is in plain words and includes a Virginia Voter Photo ID card; the statutory list is in Va. Code § 24.2-643(B). The ID rule for early voting is the same (§ 24.2-701.1(A)).

Electoral Board: the county page lists the board members with individual mailboxes, which are not recorded; no general mailbox or phone for the board was found. Its May 2026 meeting notice placed meetings at the 5th Street County Office Building, Room C. Meeting dates near an election may differ (the page says it meets more often in the two months before an election).

Permanent absentee form: the Department's page links form SBE-703.1C under the label "Permanent Absentee Application", but that PDF is the Permanent Absentee Voter Change Form for voters already on the list. Joining the list is done in Section 4 of SBE-701/703.1 or online. Leaving it can be done on SBE-703.1C (Section 6) or on ELECT-703.1D, linked from the Department's Voter Forms page. The SBE-703.1C PDF has an AcroForm with no fields, and the other form PDFs have none, so none is recorded as fillable.
Hidden page content: the county How to Vote page holds hidden video steps and a commented-out schedule for the August 4, 2026 primaries. Neither was used.

Not modeled: military and overseas (UOCAVA) voters, who may apply on the Federal Post Card Application and get ballots by email or fax, with a later return deadline (§§ 24.2-702.1, 24.2-703, 24.2-709(C)); and the details of the screen-reader ballot for print-disabled voters (§ 24.2-704(B)), which the state form offers in Section 7c.

Website terms: albemarle.org allows browsing for informational purposes but forbids redistributing or reposting its content or making derivative works without the county's written permission. County quotes here are kept to one short sentence or clause for citation; republishing page content may need permission.
Names: the county Elections page names the Director of Elections / General Registrar, and the court page names the clerk and judges; no names are recorded here.

Postmarks: the county page says a mailed ballot needs a postmark dated on or before election day", but under Va. Code § 24.2-709(A) and (B) the postmark matters only for a ballot that arrives after the polls close. Under 1VAC20-70-20(F) a ballot arriving after Election Day with a missing postmark is invalid; with an illegible postmark the registrar checks the Intelligent Mail barcode and then the date the Statement of Voter was signed.

Replacement ballots: the State Board form for a Va. Code § 24.2-703.2 replacement ballot (voters with a disability or illness whose ballot did not arrive or was lost) was not found on the Department's Absentee and Early Voting or Voter Forms pages; ask the registrar's office.

Central absentee voter precinct: Va. Code § 24.2-708 lets a voter with an unused or missing mail ballot vote at the central absentee voter precinct on Election Day, but its Albemarle location was not found on the pages read (see the local-law caveat).

Court venue: Va. Code § 24.2-706(G) says "The circuit courts shall have jurisdiction" without naming a venue. The Albemarle Circuit Court is recorded because it is the circuit court for the county; that is an inference, not something the section says.

Curbside voting: the county's curbside statement (voters 65 or older, or with a physical or mental disability) is on its Election Day page about polling places. For early voting, the Department's page says accessible equipment and curbside voting are available on request.

Form of government: Va. Code § 15.2-537 (registrars and electoral boards unaffected by the county executive form) is cited on the reading that Albemarle uses the county executive form; no page read in this check names the county's form of government.

corrections: Quotes: all 83 original quotes confirmed. The 69 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only), and each cited subsection letter matches the text. The 4 regulation quotes were matched against 1VAC20-70-20 on law.lis.virginia.gov and the Department of Elections step quote against its Absentee and Early Voting page, both re-fetched on 2026-10-11. www.albemarle.org still answered 403 on 2026-10-11 (robots.txt included) and was not bypassed, so the 9 county quotes were matched against the Internet Archive copies the file names (How to Vote 20260814172629, the latest capture; Electoral Board 20260510030231). 18 quotes were added and checked the same way: Va. Code §§ 24.2-416(A), 24.2-420.1(A), 24.2-706(B) (note whether registered), 24.2-706(C)(4) (first-time mail voter ID), 24.2-709(A) (return before polls close), 24.2-709.1(C) (two clauses: ballots received by the Friday before; errors that would void the ballot), 24.2-708(A)(1), 24.2-708(A)(3), 24.2-703.2 (two), 24.2-603, 24.2-705(A)(ii), 24.2-705(B)(1), and 1VAC20-70-20(B)(4), (B)(5), (B)(8) and (F)(3).

Summary: 'Envelope errors can be cured by then' overstated the cure. Under § 24.2-709.1(C) it covers ballots received by the Friday before the election whose errors would void them; the summary now says so, and 'by noon' is now 'before noon' (§ 24.2-709(B)).

s6: the law requires ballots to be available 'not later than 45 days prior' (§ 24.2-612); 'Ballots go out starting 45 days before' is now the law's deadline plus the Department's statement that ballots can be mailed starting 45 days before. 'Checks that you are registered in Albemarle County' is now 'notes whether you are a registered voter' (§ 24.2-706(B)); adds first-class or expedited mailing with proof (§ 24.2-706(C)) and the holding of applications received before ballots are printed (§ 24.2-701(A)).

s8: the material-omission list now follows 1VAC20-70-20(B) and (C): house number and street or rural route instead of 'street address', both city and ZIP code, a first initial accepted with a full middle name, and city or ZIP alone accepted. 'Unless it is cured' is now limited to ballots received by the Friday before the election. Adds the Statement of Voter items (§ 24.2-706(C)(2)) and the ID rule for some first-time voters who registered by mail (§ 24.2-706(C)(4); Department page), which was missing.

s9: the deadline read as if every mailed ballot needed an Election Day postmark. Any ballot received by the registrar or at a drop-off location before the polls close counts (§ 24.2-709(A)); the postmark rule applies only to mailed ballots arriving afterwards (§ 24.2-709(B)). Adds the missing and illegible postmark rule of 1VAC20-70-20(F).

s10: adds the condition in § 24.2-709.1(C) that the error or failure 'would render the ballot void by law', the three-day notice timing in the step text, and that no notice duty was found for ballots arriving after the Friday before.

s11: adds the condition that the ballot be returned unopened, or opened and unmarked, and the provisional ballot when the return cannot be confirmed (§ 24.2-708(A)(1)), the provisional ballot for a voter who goes to the polls without returning the ballot (§ 24.2-708(A)(3)), the officer-of-election route for the lost-ballot statement (§ 24.2-708(B)(1)) and the central absentee voter precinct. Adds the replacement ballot for voters with a disability or illness (§ 24.2-703.2) with its Saturday close-of-business deadline, which was missing. Poll hours now cite § 24.2-603.

s12: 'a death in the family' was broader than § 24.2-705(A), which names the hospitalization, illness or death of a spouse, child or parent, or another emergency; clause (ii) needs an emergency that occurred after the application deadline. The § 24.2-705(B) route now gives its conditions (an obligation arising after 12:00 p.m. on the Saturday before that requires absence from the county on Election Day for business, profession or occupation, the voter's or an immediate family member's hospitalization, or an immediate family member's death; or an officer of election reassigned after that time) and the § 24.2-643 ID requirement. The escalation rung for a ballot not received within 10 days uses the same family wording.

s5: 'Applications are accepted from 12 months before' is now 'may be accepted', with the later-date rule of § 24.2-701(A); adds Sections 3 and 5 of the form (Section 5 is not used with the permanent option). s4: the county's curbside statement is on its Election Day page about polling places, so it is now attributed that way, and curbside at early voting is attributed to the Department's page. s1: adds §§ 24.2-416(A) and 24.2-420.1(A) for the October 23 registration deadline and in-person same-day registration. s2: names ELECT-703.1D and Section 6 of SBE-703.1C for leaving the permanent list.

Forms: f4 (SBE-703.1C) fillable was null; its AcroForm has an empty Fields array, so it is recorded as not fillable. Added f6, ELECT-703.1D Request to Remove Name from Permanent Absentee Voter List (Rev. 5/2022), an official form linked from the Department's Voter Forms page that was missing. Form numbers and revisions for f1, f3, f4 and f5 were confirmed from the PDFs, and Sections 3, 4, 5 and 7c of f1 match the step text.

Escalation: the provisional-ballot rung said any provisional voter may send ID; under § 24.2-653(B) that applies to a voter who voted provisionally for lack of ID, while any provisional voter may attend the meeting. The cure rung is limited to ballots received by the Friday before. The lost-ballot rung adds the officer of election and the § 24.2-703.2 replacement ballot. The court rung now says that § 24.2-706(G) names no venue. The Department rung adds the complaint forms on its Voter Forms page.

Caveats: the permanent-list form caveat now records the fillable check and ELECT-703.1D; added caveats on the county's postmark wording and the missing-postmark rule, the replacement ballot form that was not located, the central absentee voter precinct location, the court venue inference, the curbside statements and the county executive form reading of § 15.2-537. Sources: added the Voter Forms page, ELECT-703.1D and §§ 24.2-416, 24.2-420.1, 24.2-703.2 and 24.2-603.
open_issues: County pages were read only from Internet Archive copies; the latest How to Vote capture is from August 14, 2026, before the September 9 deadline for posting satellite offices and drop-off sites. Any site or schedule change posted later is not reflected; the Department's live Early Voting page agrees on the September 18 to October 31 dates. Confirm on the live page or by phone.

No local ordinance is quoted: the central absentee voter precinct ordinance required by § 24.2-712(A) was not read (County Code on Municode, terms forbid automated access; no Legistar matter title found). It does not change any voter step.
The State Board form for a § 24.2-703.2 replacement ballot was not located on the Department pages read.

Early voting starts September 18 on both the county and Department pages, a day before the 45th day counted from § 24.2-701.1(A); the reason was not found in the index text. The steps follow the official schedule.
The county says a returned ballot cannot be handed to anyone, while § 24.2-707(B)(ii) allows return by the voter in person to the general registrar; recorded in caveats.
Sections 24.2-653, -653.01, -706, -709, -709.1 and -711.1 end on January 1, 2027, and § 24.2-703.1 on July 1, 2027; the index holds no later text. This does not affect the November 3, 2026 election.
